questions.q: Transform to complex: 'He was too tired to work.'
questions.a: 'He was so tired that he could not work.' 'too…to' = 'so…that + cannot'. A wrong answer 'so tired to work' loses the negative-result clause — the equivalence breaks.

questions.q: Make it simple: 'Although he was ill, he attended the meeting.'
questions.a: 'In spite of his illness, he attended the meeting' (or 'Despite being ill…'). A wrong answer keeping 'although' shows the student renamed rather than restructured — the clause must shrink to a phrase.

questions.q: Transform: 'If you do not study, you will fail' → using 'unless'.
questions.a: 'Unless you study, you will fail.' 'unless' = 'if not' — the negation moves into the connector. A wrong answer 'unless you do not study' double-negates the condition.
